summary: RFC 5785 defines the /.well-known/ path prefix for http and https. This memo formally updates RFC 6455 so the same well-known URI mechanism can also be used with the ws and wss URI schemes of the WebSocket Protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: There was a standard place on web servers for finding info about the site. This says WebSocket addresses can use that same place.

questions: are well-known uris available for ws and wss
subtitle: The /.well-known/ URI mechanism now formally applies to ws and wss WebSocket URIs.

tldr.problem: RFC 5785 defined the /.well-known/ path prefix for http and https, but RFC 6455 did not define its use for the ws and wss schemes.
tldr.mechanism: This memo formally updates RFC 6455 to extend well-known URIs to ws and wss, sharing the existing registry of URI suffixes.
tldr.outcome: No IANA registry changes are needed, but WebSocket-specific well-known suffixes need extra security thought.

today: RFC 8307 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 6455. It has not been obsoleted or updated by a later RFC.

sections.title: Extending Well-Known URIs
sections.content:
RFC 5785 defines the path prefix /.well-known and an IANA registry of URI suffixes. It was specifically defined for the http and https schemes, and other schemes such as coap and coaps have since adopted it, sharing the same registry.

RFC 6455 defines the ws and wss schemes for the WebSocket Protocol but did not define well-known URIs for them. This memo updates RFC 6455 to allow it.
sections.plainLanguage: Websites keep a special shelf for standard notes. WebSocket addresses are now allowed to use the shelf too.

sections.title: Registry and IANA
sections.content: Well-known URIs for ws and wss share the URI suffix registry established by RFC 5785. The memo needs no change to the registry or its IANA considerations, and this document requires no IANA actions.
sections.plainLanguage: Everyone uses the same list of shelf labels, so no new list is needed.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The security considerations of RFC 5785 apply to all well-known URIs. It was always possible to form ws and wss URIs that map to well-known HTTP(S) URIs using the procedure in Section 4 of RFC 6455, so no new considerations arise from formalizing this.

Applications that define well-known suffixes specifically for WebSocket use should also consider whether the resources exposed under the equivalent HTTP(S) URI pose information disclosure or other security risks.
sections.plainLanguage: Putting a note on the shelf is fine, but check that the note does not reveal secrets.

references.text: Nottingham, M. and E. Hammer-Lahav, "Defining Well-Known Uniform Resource Identifiers (URIs)", RFC 5785, April 2010.
Fette, I. and A. Melnikov, "The WebSocket Protocol", RFC 6455, December 2011.
